regression_power.rationale: Once the acceptance suite is out of the picture, breaking any covered behaviour — i.e. all of it — fails nothing. A single sign flip in compareRows or reordering the debounce effects in home.tsx ships undetected.

evidence: app/app — no tests, hence no padding or noise
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no low-value tests; per the rubric this is neutral, though the value a lean suite over format.ts and compareRows would have added is real.

findings.issue: No test runner, no test script, and no test files — the whole app depends on the harness-owned acceptance suite
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (or @react-router/dev's test tooling) and a 'test' script; start with unit tests for format.ts, data.server.ts helpers, and the home/pokemon loader logic

findings.issue: Filter pipeline, page clamping and pagination slicing are pure-ish logic with no coverage; deep-link URL-state contract (q/type/generation/page defaults, page reset on filter change) is only guarded by the external suite
findings.suggestion: Extract filtering/pagination into a testable function and add cases for combined filters, empty results, page > totalPages, and default-parameter omission

findings.issue: compareRows implements missing-values-last in both sort directions plus numeric/string dispatch; a one-character change inverts it and nothing fails
findings.suggestion: Unit-test ascending/descending on each column with missing values present, and the default level-up (level, then name) ordering

findings.issue: latestEnglishFlavorText picks the LAST English entry with whitespace collapse; easy to regress to first entry or wrong language match
findings.suggestion: Unit tests with multi-language entries, \n/\f whitespace, and no-English cases

findings.issue: Promise cache with rejection-eviction and mixed key schemes (lowercased name vs raw URL) is untested; stale-error or key-collision bugs surface only when API data changes
findings.suggestion: Unit tests: rejected loads are evicted and retried; same resource by name and URL share cache correctly

findings.issue: refId regex parsing plus the id>10000 alternate-form exclusion duplicated at data.server.ts:109, home.tsx:51, ability.tsx:24, type.tsx:47 — four sites that can drift independently
findings.suggestion: Centralize the exclusion in one helper and test it against form URLs like /pokemon/10033/

findings.issue: Default game = highest order and method ordering (Level Up, Machine, Egg, Tutor, then alphabetical) are untested pure logic
findings.suggestion: Loader-level tests with a small fixture Pokémon asserting game selection from ?game= and fallback, and method table order

findings.issue: Empty state keys on cards.length instead of total; an enrichment failure would render 'No Pokémon found' beside a nonzero count
findings.suggestion: Branch on total === 0; add a test asserting the count message and list are consistent

findings.issue: HashScroller uses two setTimeouts (0/100 ms) to work around hydration timing; no test would catch it breaking when data loading timings change
findings.suggestion: A route-level test asserting /pokemon/pikachu#moves scrolls to #moves, or use ScrollRestoration's hash handling if sufficient

findings.issue: The notFound contract (loader flag + per-route render branch + meta branch) is duplicated across five routes; one route dropping its branch fails silently
findings.suggestion: Throw a 404 Response from loaders so the root ErrorBoundary centralizes handling, and test one unknown name per resource type

summary: The app contains zero tests and no test infrastructure; everything rests on the harness's acceptance suite. The most regression-prone code — home filtering/pagination/URL state, move-table sorting, English-name/flavor-text selection, the caching layer, and the quadruple-duplicated alternate-form exclusion — has no owned guard. Any refactor of the data layer or loaders after merge would ship bugs undetected.
